name: English square cut beard

card.summary: A full beard groomed into a squared-off shape, used to give the lower face a broader, more angular outline and the impression of a stronger jaw.
card.aka: square cut beard, squared full beard
card.note: Style name is used in grooming media; research on beards is about beardedness in general rather than this cut.

quick.overview:
The English square cut beard is a full beard trimmed so its lower edge and sides look squared rather than rounded or pointed. The appeal is a broader, more defined lower-face outline.

Research on beards in general reports that facial hair increases perceived jaw size and is associated in studies with perceptions of dominance and masculinity, and that the interaction between facial masculinity and beardedness affects ratings of attractiveness. No study has specifically tested this cut.
quick.how: People grow a full beard and then trim the cheek line, neckline and bottom edge to the desired shape, typically with trimmers and a barber's visits. Growth takes weeks to months, and the squared edge needs regular upkeep as hair grows out.
quick.risks: Beards can be itchy or patchy during growth, and patchy growth limits whether a full squared outline is possible. Skin irritation from trimming and ingrown hairs are common grooming issues.

lead: The English square cut beard is a name for a full beard shaped with a squared outline. Full-beard styles in general are described as showing full, unmodified growth over the cheeks, chin, moustache and neck, with variants distinguished by how the hair is shaped [1].

People use beard shaping to alter the apparent proportions of the lower face. Wikipedia's article on beards notes that beards are linked in evolutionary psychology to signalling sexual maturity and dominance because they increase perceived jaw size, and that scholars disagree on whether they evolved mainly through attractiveness or male competition [2].

Research on how beards are perceived includes studies such as a 2016 paper on how facial masculinity and beardedness interact in women's ratings of male attractiveness [3]. These studies concern beards generally, not this particular cut.

chain: Full beard grown over the lower face
Edges squared off to a broad, angular outline
Jaw and lower face look wider and more defined
angle.text: A beard adds hair volume along the jaw, and a squared outline emphasises width and angles. Beards in general are reported to increase perceived jaw size [2].

infobox: Full cheek, chin and neck growth [1]
Garibaldi beard (even extension below the chin) [1]

paras: The full beard is the base from which many styles are made, with the Garibaldi beard, named after Giuseppe Garibaldi, described as extending evenly below the chin [1]. A square cut shapes the same growth into a more geometric silhouette. Beards have a long history of cultural meaning, from ancient symbols of sovereignty to Greek associations with virility, and fashion has cycled between bearded and clean-shaven eras [2].
No studies found. Studies of beard perception in general, for example on how beardedness interacts with facial masculinity in attractiveness ratings, are listed in the research literature [3].
